title: OpenAI Announces Introduction of Third-Party Independent Safety Assessments in the Early Stages of AI Model Development
excerpt: Amid growing concerns about the potential risks of artificial intelligence, OpenAI has recently announced its latest developments in safety governance. Accordin
content_html:
Amid growing concerns about the potential risks of artificial intelligence, OpenAI has recently announced its latest developments in safety governance. According to reports, the company plans to break away from the traditional internal closed-loop testing model and formally involve third-party independent organizations at an earlier stage in the AI model development cycle, conducting systematic safety risk assessments.

To ensure that this innovative mechanism can truly play an effective role, OpenAI has also clearly outlined the core priorities for the successful implementation of external evaluations. These include four key pillars: a strong independent operational mechanism, strict adherence to scientific rigor, implementation of robust daily safety practices, and clear and well-defined safety responsibilities among all parties involved.

This move indicates that as the iteration speed of cutting-edge artificial intelligence models continues to accelerate, leading companies in the industry are proactively opening up to the outside, working together with objective and impartial third-party forces to build a security defense, thereby addressing the long-term scrutiny of the public and regulatory authorities on the controllability of technology.
